title: Magit post-stage hook and bridge wrapper command identity

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

mechanism: `magit-run-post-stage-hook' uses command identity, so a direct function call inside a wrapper can have correct Git effects but different Magit semantics.
hypothesis: Calling `magit-run-post-stage-hook' while `this-command' is a bridge wrapper should not run `magit-post-stage-hook`; setting `this-command' to a recognized staging command should run it.

sources.name: magit post-refresh hook includes post-stage runner

minimal_fixture: Magit loaded from the installed Straight build; no Git repository is mutated.
predicted_behavior: Hook execution depends on `this-command', independent of whether lower-level Git state was already changed.

independent_checks.name: wrapper command did not trigger post-stage hook

counterexample: A wrapper command that calls Magit lower-level functions can pass an index checker while skipping package hooks.
derived_gym_requirement: Faithful Magit actions must either enter through a recognized command path or explicitly model and test the command identity consequences.
